plan.english: A guest arrived at the house; he was thirsty and tired. The master caught sight of him and said to him: 'Sit down, guest! Eat the meat and drink the wine!' He, sitting, ate and drank. Then sleep seized him. At dawn he stood up and went away. Then the master gave him a gift.

The guest ate and drank. Then he said: 'Guest, now you are satisfied. Who are you? Where are you going? Is your mother alive?' 'I am the son of a shepherd. I am going to my brother's house. My mother is alive; my father is not.' 'Lie down in my dwelling, and the night will bring you rest.' Then he lay down.

The mistress seated the guest and carried water to him. Then he became cold. She clothed him in wool, and he became warm. Then she prepared something nourishing and cooked the meat. Then the guest said: 'This house is dear to me. May it stand for many years!'

'Whose son are you?' 'I am the son of your father's guest.' 'He ate in my dwelling. This house gave him a horse, and he gave a cart. Now I know you, and you are dear to me. Eat at my fire, and I will give you a gift. The bond between the two houses will not break.'

Last year the master gave the guest a yoke. Yesterday the guest came again to the master's house, carrying a gift. Then he looked at it, became joyful, and spoke: 'A gift went out from my house, and a gift has come again to my house. Sit down, and eat together.' Then the two ate.

The two fathers sat down together and drank wine. This one gave that one a plough; that one gave this one a boat. Then this one said: 'Let there be a bond between the two houses. May our sons be friends. Let no one break the pledge.'

The guest is dear to the gods. Whoever kills his own guest is a wolf and not a man. No one will give him fire, water and a seat. The wolf has no dwelling. Who protects him? Sky protects him. The gods have seen him.

It was getting dark, and a guest arrived at the king's house. Then the king stood up, took hold of his arm and led him inside and seated him on a seat. Then the queen carried meat and honey to him. Then he ate and was sated. The king said: 'Lie down. When the dawn has shone, tell me your name.'

title: A blessing for the guest on the path

plan.english: Father Sky, you who protect the guest, guard him on the path. Mother Earth, carry him. May his path be straight, and may the star show him the path, and may the sun warm him. May the wolf not seize him. May he come to his own house, and may his mother see him.

title: The rock at the edge of the field

plan.english: The guest stood up, and the master went with him and spoke: 'This rock stands in my field; that path is yours. Go in peace. Remember this house. When you come again to my house, I will honor you.'

title: An oath by Father Sky and Mother Earth

plan.english: Father Sky, hear me! Mother Earth, listen! I did not steal my kinsman's horse. If I speak a lie, may you strike me down, Sky, and may the earth not nourish me. If I speak the truth, may I live and see the dawn, and may my house stand.

The man sat down at the fire and made the oath. 'The sun has seen me, the fire heard me, the water knows me. I did not steal the cart. If I speak a lie, may the fire burn me, may the water swallow me, and may the sun not catch sight of me.'

title: The man who broke his oath

plan.english: A man made an oath and broke it. The gods saw him. Then his barley vanished, his house fell and his offspring was gone. Then death seized him, and no one honored him. Fire guards the oath. A man dies; an oath does not die.
'Will you make the oath?' 'I will make it.' 'Whom do you fear?' 'I fear Father Sky. He has seen what is hidden. If I lie to him, may he strike me down, and may my offspring not grow.'

Master, listen to my pledge! I will guard your sheep for a year. I will lead them to the water and drive them home at night, and at night I will stay awake, and I will work for you. If a wolf seizes a sheep, I will give you a sheep. If I lie to you, may the gods strike me down. Give me my wage.

King, I shall speak the truth. I saw a man leading a dog from the field, with these eyes. He is not my brother, and I am not his friend. What I saw, that I say. If I speak a lie, may my eyes not see the sun, and may the dawn not grow bright for me.

Whoever breaks this oath: may it not rain on his field; may his barley not grow; may his daughters be gone; may fire burn his house; may Perkwunos strike him down; may sleep not come to him; and may no one honor his name. Whoever guards it, may his house stand.

King, I have made this pledge: I will go forward. May I not flee. I shall die, or I shall win imperishable fame. Sky, you have seen me. If I flee, may the earth swallow me. My name will become famous.

Two brothers were before the king. This one said: 'These cattle are mine.' That one said: 'They are not yours; they are mine.' Then he said: 'Cattle know their own master. Cry out to them, you two!' Then this one cried out, and they did not go. That one cried out, and they heard his voice and went to him. Then he said to that one: 'They are yours.'

title: The sheep that was to be split

plan.english: Two women went to the king and said: 'The sheep is mine.' Then he said: 'Shepherd, split the sheep in two!' Then this one said: 'Split it.' That one cried out: 'Do not split it! Let it be this one's, and let it live.' Then he said: 'You are its mistress. Take it.'

Two kinsmen went to the king. This one had killed that one's dog. Then he said: 'If a stranger kills a dog, let him give two dogs. If a brother kills a brother's dog, let him give a dog. Do for him what is proper.' Then the two became brothers again.

A woman went to the king and said: 'My horse is gone.' Then he said to the shepherd: 'Track it.' Then the shepherd tracked it along the path and found it in the enclosure of a man. Then he said: 'How is the horse in your enclosure?' 'I found it on the path.' 'Did you speak to the woman?' 'I did not speak to her.' 'Give it to the woman again. Whoever finds and does not speak, he steals.'

The father-in-law and the son-in-law were before the king. The father-in-law said: 'He did not bring me the bride price.' 'Son-in-law, did you give the bride price?' 'I gave ten cattle.' 'Who saw it?' 'I saw it.' 'Son-in-law, you have spoken the truth. Father-in-law, you spoke a lie. Honor your son-in-law.'

A man went to the king and spoke: 'My brother's cattle ate my barley. What shall he give me?' Then he said: 'Let him give you barley, and let him build a hedge. A hedge guards peace.' Then he built the hedge.

Kinsmen, listen to my word! Whoever steals a plough, let him give three ploughs. Whoever steals a cart, let him bring six carts. Whoever burns a house, let him build five houses. Whoever kills a free man, let him give a hundred cattle. Whoever kills the king, let him give a thousand cattle. And if he does not give, I shall seize his dwelling.

This one broke that one's boat. Then the king said: 'If anyone takes the boat of his own brother and the boat sinks, let him give him a boat. If the brother gave it and it sinks, let him not give anything. The boat is the brother's.'

For many years there was a fight between the two houses. Then the two came together. This one said to that one: 'Your brother killed my offspring, and my brother killed your offspring. Take the price, and I too will take the price. Peace will be for us.' Then they drank wine together.

title: Brother and brother in the field

plan.english: Two twins were in the field. 'Kinsman, what are we seeking?' 'We seek our father's field.' 'Great is the field, and we two are brothers. May I not hit my own brother! Mother Earth feeds us two.' Then that one said: 'You have spoken the truth. Let us sit down and drink together.' Then the two sat down, and drank.

The two kings met on the mountain. Then this one said: 'There was a fight between our houses. Let there be peace for us. May the sun see us. Whoever breaks the pledge, let death seize him.' Then that one said: 'I make the pledge, and may it stand.' Then the two settlements became friends.

The two sons rose against one another. Then the mother stood up between them and spoke: 'You are born of me. I nourished you. Sons, hit me! Let no one kill his own brother.' Then the two heard her and sat down on the earth. Peace came to them.

The fight between the two houses was great. Then the two sat down together. 'Give your daughter to my son, and I will give you the bride price, ten horses.' 'I give you my daughter. My daughter will be your daughter-in-law. Let us be kin.' Then the fight vanished.
Kinsmen, listen! The fight devoured men. Let the earth cover the slain, and let peace be a shelter for you. Let the fight lie down. Lift the plough and plough the field. May the two households live.
Sky protects the guest. Honor him, and the gods honor you. Fire warms the guest, and the house feeds him. Whoever drives the guest away drives the gods away. Who knows? A guest may be a god.
A true word stands; a lie falls. It is straight; the lie is curved. A man's word is his bond. Good fame follows the true word.

Whoever steals, night hides him; the sun has seen him. Whoever drives off horses, the dog knows him. The wolf comes in the night; the shepherd stays awake. The man who steals eats and is not satisfied.
A gift seeks a gift. Whoever gives receives; whoever does not give does not receive. A gift does not vanish. A gift from a good heart is dear. The giver of good things is dear.
A brother is a brother's arm. Whoever kills his brother cuts off his own arm. A man has two arms, a house has two brothers. A lone sheep is the wolf's meat.
The yoke joins two horses; the two run together; the pledge joins two houses. If the pledge breaks, a fight comes to the two. Guard the pledge.

A king is a shepherd of men. The shepherd guards the sheep from the wolf; the king protects them from the lie. The king's word is a straight path. Whoever makes the word straight, he is a king. Whoever speaks a curved word is not a king.
Cattle die, kin die, a man dies. Good fame does not die. Whoever wins good fame, his name lives. The sun comes again; he does not come again.
